title: Watching the Watchers
text:
Many people now carry smartphones everywhere they go. These devices record location data, search history, and the apps people use each day. Companies often collect this information to show users advertisements that match their interests. Although most users accept these terms without reading them, the data can reveal far more about a person's life than they expect.

Governments also use surveillance technology, including cameras in public spaces and tools that analyze internet traffic. Supporters argue that these systems help prevent crime and find missing people. Critics, however, warn that constant monitoring can threaten freedom of expression and make citizens feel watched even when they have done nothing wrong. Finding the right balance between security and privacy remains a difficult challenge.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what do companies often collect?
options: Data to show ads that match users' interests

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what do supporters say government surveillance systems help to do?
options: Prevent crime and find missing people

questions.text: What can be inferred about users who accept terms without reading them?
options: They may not realize how much personal information is shared
They understand every detail of the data collection
They prefer to receive no advertisements at all
They are legally required to read the terms

questions.text: What is the author's attitude toward the balance between security and privacy?
options: They see it as a difficult problem with no easy answer
They think privacy is completely unimportant
They are certain that security always wins
They think surveillance has no effect on citizens

public messages that promote a product or service
watching and checking something over a period of time
people who publicly disagree with or question something

paragraph_translations: Muchas personas llevan ahora teléfonos inteligentes a todas partes. Estos dispositivos registran datos de ubicación, el historial de búsqueda y las aplicaciones que las personas usan cada día. Las empresas suelen recopilar esta información para mostrar a los usuarios anuncios que coinciden con sus intereses. Aunque la mayoría de los usuarios acepta estas condiciones sin leerlas, los datos pueden revelar mucho más sobre la vida de una persona de lo que esperan.

Los gobiernos también usan tecnología de vigilancia, incluidas cámaras en espacios públicos y herramientas que analizan el tráfico de internet. Quienes la apoyan afirman que estos sistemas ayudan a prevenir delitos y a encontrar personas desaparecidas. Los críticos, sin embargo, advierten que la vigilancia constante puede amenazar la libertad de expresión y hacer que los ciudadanos se sientan observados incluso cuando no han hecho nada malo. Encontrar el equilibrio adecuado entre seguridad y privacidad sigue siendo un desafío difícil.
